title: The Nose
description: On the twenty-fifth of March a St Petersburg barber finds a nose in his breakfast loaf. Its owner, Major Kovaloff, wakes to a smooth blank, and spends two weeks chasing a nose that now wears the uniform of a state councillor.
source_title: The Nose, in The Mantle and Other Stories, translated by Claud Field

cover.alt: Kovaloff sees his own nose step out of a carriage in uniform
cover.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A nose in the loaf
elements.text: Ivan Jakovlevitch cuts his morning bread and finds a nose he recognises: Kovaloff's, whom he shaves on Sundays and Wednesdays. His wife throws him out with it.

metadata.source_quote: He put in his finger, and drew out--a nose!

image.alt: The barber finds a nose in his breakfast loaf
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: On the Isaac Bridge
elements.text: He tries to drop the nose, wrapped in a rag, anywhere at all, and finally throws it from the Isaac Bridge into the Neva, under the eye of a police inspector.

image.alt: On the Isaac Bridge the barber tries to rid himself of the nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A smooth vacancy
elements.text: Major Kovaloff wakes, reaches for his mirror to look at a pimple, and finds his face perfectly flat.

metadata.source_quote: instead of his nose he had a perfectly smooth vacancy in his face.

image.alt: Kovaloff wakes to find a smooth blank where his nose was
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The nose in uniform
elements.text: A carriage stops; a gentleman in a gold-embroidered uniform and a plumed hat hurries up some steps. It is his nose.

metadata.source_quote: it held the rank of a state-councillor.

image.alt: Kovaloff sees his own nose step out of a carriage in uniform
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: I am myself
elements.text: Kovaloff corners his nose in front of a shop at the Bazar and timidly asks it to return. The nose denies any connection and walks off.

metadata.source_quote: I am myself. Besides, there can be no close relations between us.

image.alt: Kovaloff begs his nose to return; it denies they are related
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The advertisement office
elements.text: No police chief is at home, so Kovaloff tries the newspaper. The clerk refuses the notice in case it makes the paper look ridiculous, and offers him snuff.

metadata.source_quote: It is perfectly flat like a freshly fried pancake.

image.alt: Kovaloff tries to advertise for his lost nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Madame Podtotchina
elements.text: Kovaloff decides that a colonel's wife has bewitched him because he would not marry her daughter, and writes to accuse her. Her innocent reply convinces him.

image.alt: Madame Podtotchina and her daughter read Kovaloff's accusing letter
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Arrested on the road to Riga
elements.text: A police officer brings the nose back, wrapped in paper: it was caught boarding a coach for Riga with a passport in an official's name.

metadata.source_quote: It has been arrested just as it was getting into a carriage for Riga.

image.alt: A police officer brings back the nose wrapped in paper
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: It will not stick
elements.text: The nose falls off his face like a cork. The doctor declines to help and offers to buy it in a jar.

image.alt: The doctor refuses to reattach the nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Rumours on the Nevsky
elements.text: The city hears that the Major's nose takes a walk on the Nevsky Avenue at three o'clock every day. Crowds gather and a speculator rents out benches.

metadata.source_quote: Major Kovaloff's nose was to be seen walking every day at three o'clock on the Neffsky Avenue.

image.alt: Crowds on the Nevsky hoping to see the Major's nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The seventh of April
elements.text: One morning the nose is simply back between his cheeks. Kovaloff struts down the Nevsky as if nothing had happened.

image.alt: The seventh of April: the nose is back
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Such cases do occur
elements.text: The narrator complains that the story is improbable and useless, and concludes that such things happen anyway.

metadata.source_quote: such cases do occur--rarely, it is true, but now and then actually.

image.alt: The seventh of April: the nose is back
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Major Kovaloff
elements.text: A collegiate assessor who calls himself Major, walks the Nevsky daily, wears many seals and hopes for a vice-governorship and a rich wife.

metadata.source_quote: go to my house in Sadovaia Street and ask 'Does Major Kovaloff live here?'

image.alt: Kovaloff wakes to find a smooth blank where his nose was
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Nose
elements.text: Kovaloff's nose, now a state councillor in uniform, who pays calls by carriage, carries a passport and will not acknowledge its owner.

image.alt: Kovaloff sees his own nose step out of a carriage in uniform
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Ivan Jakovlevitch
elements.text: The barber who finds the nose: unshaven, snuff-taking, given to drink and terrified of the police.

metadata.source_quote: Ivan Jakovlevitch was a terrible drunkard

image.alt: The barber finds a nose in his breakfast loaf
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Praskovia Ossipovna
elements.text: The barber's wife, fond of coffee and quick to call her husband a scoundrel.

image.alt: The barber finds a nose in his breakfast loaf
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The police officer
elements.text: The whiskered inspector from the bridge, who returns the nose and accepts a banknote for his trouble.

image.alt: A police officer brings back the nose wrapped in paper
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The doctor
elements.text: A splendidly whiskered physician with five toothbrushes, who refuses to reattach the nose on principle and offers to buy it.

image.alt: The doctor refuses to reattach the nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Madame Podtotchina
elements.text: A colonel's wife with a marriageable daughter, wrongly suspected of having spirited away the nose.

image.alt: Madame Podtotchina and her daughter read Kovaloff's accusing letter
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: St Petersburg
elements.text: The northern capital: the Nevsky Avenue, the Isaac Bridge over the Neva, the Bazar, the newspaper office, the Sadovaia Street flat.

image.alt: Kovaloff on the Nevsky Avenue
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Nevsky Avenue
elements.text: The great boulevard where everyone who matters takes a daily walk, and where the nose is rumoured to stroll at three.

image.alt: Crowds on the Nevsky hoping to see the Major's nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The barber's room
elements.text: A shop on the Ascension Avenue whose sign shows a soaped cheek and offers blood-letting.

image.alt: The barber finds a nose in his breakfast loaf
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Table of Ranks
elements.text: Fourteen grades of state service. Kovaloff is a collegiate assessor, eighth grade; his nose wears the uniform of the fifth.

image.alt: Kovaloff sees his own nose step out of a carriage in uniform
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Rumour and magnetism
elements.text: A city ready to believe in wonders, recently thrilled by experiments in magnetism and stories of floating chairs.

metadata.source_quote: the public had recently been impressed by experiments in magnetism.

image.alt: Crowds on the Nevsky hoping to see the Major's nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Rank as identity
elements.text: Kovaloff fears losing face more than losing his nose. The nose's real offence is to outrank him.

image.alt: Kovaloff begs his nose to return; it denies they are related
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The absurd as routine
elements.text: Every institution treats the impossible as a matter of procedure: the clerk, the doctor and the police each have a form for it.

image.alt: Kovaloff tries to advertise for his lost nose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: A story without a reason
elements.text: The narrator's closing complaints make the lack of explanation part of the joke.

image.alt: The seventh of April: the nose is back
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Northern Bee
elements.text: The newspaper clerk suggests the case be written up as a natural curiosity for the Northern Bee, a real St Petersburg paper of the time.

metadata.source_quote: publish the article in the Northern Bee

elements.title: Animal magnetism
elements.text: The story's rumour-hungry city has recently been impressed by experiments in magnetism, Mesmer's fashionable pseudo-science.

elements.title: Kazan Cathedral and the censor
elements.text: In Gogol's manuscript Kovaloff finds his nose praying in Kazan Cathedral; the censors would not allow it, and the scene moved to a shopping arcade. Readers who know the later text may picture it there.

elements.title: Slawkenbergius's Tale (Sterne, Tristram Shandy)
elements.text: Laurence Sterne's comic tale of a stranger with an enormous nose who throws a whole city into uproar. Readers may see it as the comic ancestor of Gogol's nose.

elements.title: The Double (Dostoevsky, 1846)
elements.text: A timid clerk meets a successful copy of himself who takes over his career. Readers may see Golyadkin's double as Kovaloff's nose grown into a whole person.

elements.title: The Metamorphosis (Kafka, 1915)
elements.text: A salesman wakes as an insect and worries about his job. Readers may set it beside The Nose as the other great story of an impossible morning met with paperwork.

elements.title: The Nose (Shostakovich, 1930)
elements.text: Dmitri Shostakovich's first opera, written at twenty-two, with a nose that sings and an interlude for percussion alone. Readers may hear the story's absurdity as music.

elements.title: The Master and Margarita (Bulgakov)
elements.text: The devil visits Moscow and the city's officials handle magic as a bureaucratic nuisance. Readers may think of Gogol, whom Bulgakov revered, behind every deadpan absurdity.

elements.title: Pinocchio (Collodi, 1883)
elements.text: A puppet whose nose grows when he lies. Readers may set it in contrast: Pinocchio's nose betrays him, Kovaloff's abandons him.

elements.title: Surrealism
elements.text: The movement of André Breton and Salvador Dalí, which put dream logic into painting and film. Readers may see Gogol's walking nose as a surrealist image eighty years early.

elements.title: Cyrano de Bergerac (Rostand, 1897)
elements.text: A brilliant swordsman ashamed of his huge nose. Readers may think of him as the opposite of Kovaloff: one man too much nose, the other none, both sure the nose decides how they are seen.
